Likewise, although ΔEITP outperforms other color difference metrics on Database 4 (Table 5), its performance is statistically equivalent to the other color difference metrics. One of the reasons that the performance of ΔEITP is not superior for Database 4 could be because the size of the database is relatively small (96 images). In addition, Database 4 was the one where all the metrics underperformed, possibly as a result of the widely varying color distortions requiring a more advanced model than averaging across the entire image without any frequency-weighting. Conclusion and Future Work In this paper, we evaluate several color difference metrics to assess the quality of HDR content. In particular, we consider the two most commonly used color difference metrics: ΔE00 and ΔE94. Additionally, we evaluate the performance of two color difference metrics designed with HDR/WCG content in mind: ΔEz and ΔEITP. We use five different databases containing a wide variety of distortions for evaluation and show that overall, ΔEITP outperforms the other color difference metrics on four out of five databases.
